annotations.title: If your iniquitie.
annotations.text: [1] No maruel that many now a daies deduce falſe and deteſtable concluſions out of this Apoſtles high and hard writings, ſeing that S. Peter [2] noted it in his daies, and him ſelf here confeſſeth that his preaching and ſpeaches were then falſely miſconſtrued: as though he had taught that the Iewes and Gentils il life and incredulity had been directly the cauſe of Gods more mercie, and that therfore ſinne commeth of God to the aduancement of his glorie, and conſequently that men might or ſhould doe il, that good might enſue thereof. Vvhich blaſphemous conſtructions they tooke of theſe and the like vvordes: [3] where ſinne abounded, there did grace more abound. and, [4] The Lawe entered in, that ſinne might abound. and out of the Pſalme 50. That thou maieſt be iuſtified in thy vvordes, and ouercome when thou art iudged. As though he meant that men do ſinne, to the end that God may be iuſtified. And at al theſe and the like places of the Apoſtle though forevvarned by S. Peter, and by the Apoſtles owne defenſe and Proteſtation, that he neuer meant ſuch horrible things, yet the vvicked alſo of this time do ſtumble and fall. [5] But the true meaning is in al ſuch places, that God can and doth when it pleaſeth him, conuert thoſe ſinnes which man committeth againſt him and his commaundements, to his glorie: though the ſinnes them ſelues ſtand not with his wil, intention, nor honour, but be directly againſt the ſame, and therfore may not be committed that any good may fall. for, what good ſo euer accidentally falleth, it proceedeth not of the ſinne, but of Gods mercie that can pardon, and of his omnipotencie that can turne it to good. And therfore againſt thoſe carnal interpretations, S. Paul very carefully & diligently giueth reaſon alſo in this place v. 6, that it is impoſſible: becauſe God could not iuſtly puniſh any man, nor ſit in iudgement at the later day for ſinne vvithout plaine iniurie, if either him ſelf vvould haue ſinne committed, or man might doe it to his glorie. Therfore let al ſincere readers of the Scriptures, and ſpecially of S. Pauls vvritings, hold this for a certaintie, as the Apoſtles owne defenſe (vvhatſoeuer he ſeeme to ſay hereafter ſounding in their ſenſe, that ſinne commeth of God, or may therfore be committed that he may vvorke good thereof) that the Apoſtle him ſelf condemneth that ſenſe as ſlaunderous and blaſphemous.

The sense of the places that found, as if God caused sinne.

annotations.title: Not any iuſt.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Theſe general ſpeeches, that both Iewe and Gentile be in ſinne, and none at all juſt, are not ſo to be taken, that none in neither ſort vvere euer good: the Scriptures expreſly ſaying that Job <mn>[2]</mn>, <mn>[3]</mn> Zacharie, Eliſabeth, and ſuch like, were juſt before God, & it vvere blaſphemie to ſay that theſe words alleged out of the 13. Pſalm, vvere meant in Chriſt's mother, in S. Iohn the Baptiſt, in the Apoſtles &c. For, this only is the ſenſe: that neither by the lawe of nature, nor lawe of Moyſes, could any man be juſt or auoid ſuch ſins as here be reckoned, but by faith and the grace of God, by which there were a number in all ages (ſpecially among the Jews) that were juſt and holy, vvhom theſe words touch not, being ſpoken only to the multitude of the vvicked, vvhich the Prophet maketh as it vvere a ſeueral body conſpiring againſt Chriſt, and perſecuting the juſt and godly, of vvhich ill companie he ſaith, that none vvas juſt nor feared God.

annotations.title: By the vvorkes of the Lawe.
annotations.text: ◦ S. Hierom and S. Chryſoſtom expound this of the ceremonial workes only, and in that ſenſe the Apoſtle ſpecially proteſteth this propoſition in his Epiſtle to the Galatians: but it is true alſo of al mans moral workes done vvithout faith & the grace of God: which can not be acceptable or auailable in Gods ſight, to iuſtifie any man, And ſo S. Auguſtine taketh it de Sp. & lit. c. 8. to. 3.

notes.text: No workes auaile without faith and grace.

annotations.title: Iuſtice of God.
annotations.text: [1] Bevvare of the wicked and vaine commentarie of the Calviniſts, gloſing, the iuſtice of God to be that which is reſident in Chriſt, apprehended by our faith: and ſo that imputed to vs vvhich we indeed haue not. Vvherein at once they haue forged themſelves againſt God's manifeſt word, a new no iuſtice, a phantaſtical apprehenſion of that which is not, a falſe faith and vntrue imputation. Whereas the iuſtice of God here, is that vvherevvith he endueth a man at his firſt conuerſion, and is now in a man, and therefore man's iuſtice: but yet God's iuſtice alſo, becauſe it is of God. Of this iuſtice in vs, vvhereby vve be truly iuſtified and indeed made juſt, S. Auguſtine [2] ſpeaketh thus: The grace of Chriſt doth vvorke our illumination and iuſtification invvardly alſo. And againe, [3] He giueth to the faithful the moſt ſecrete grace of his Spirit, which ſecretly he poureth into infants alſo. And againe, They are iuſtified in Chriſt that believe in him through the ſecrete communication and inſpiration of ſpiritual grace, whereby euery one leaneth to our Lord. And againe, He maketh juſt renevving by the Spirit, and regeneration by grace.

notes.text: The Heretics' phantastical or imputative justice.

annotations.title: By faith vvithout workes.
annotations.text: This is the place whereupon the Proteſtants gather falſly their only faith, and vvhich they commonly auouch, as though the Apoſtle ſaid, that only faith doth iuſtifie. [1] Where he both in wordes and meaning excepteth only the vvorkes, of the Lawe done without Chriſt before our conuerſion: neither excluding the Sacraments of Baptiſme or Penance, nor hope and charitie, or other Chriſtian vertues, al vvhich be the iuſtice of faith. as the good vvorkes proceding thereof, be likevviſe the lawe and iuſtice of faith. Al vvhich the Aduerſaries vvould exclude by foiſting in the terme, only. Of which kind of men S. Auguſtine [2] vpon this place de grat. & fide thus: Men not vnderſtanding that which the Apoſtle ſaith, (we counte a man to be iuſtified by faith vvithout the vvorkes of the Lawe) did thinke that he ſaid, faith would ſuffiſe a man though he liued il and had no good workes. Which God forbid the veſſel of election ſhould thinke: who in a certaine place after he had ſaid, [3] In Chriſt IESVS neither circumciſion nor prepuce auaileth any whit, he ſtraight added, but faith which worketh by loue.
